newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Superclub declines comment on Philips tie.
newsitem.headline: Superclub declines comment on Philips tie.

text.p: Superclub, a largely Belgian-centred entertainments subsidiary of Philips Electronics NV, declined to comment on a Belgian newspaper report that the Dutch company wanted to wind up its distribution activities.
"I can neither confirm nor deny the report in the (Belgian) Financieel-Economische Tijd newspaper," said a spokeswoman for Superclub, speaking by telephone from Bornem in Belgium.
"I can only say that there will be a meeting of the 120 or so Superclub staff working at Bornem tomorrow, and after that there will be a press statement if necessary," she added.
Superclub sells and rents videotapes as well as selling audio CDs, computer games and multi-media entertainment packages such as CD-interactive and CD-Roms, with a total staff of 540.
The spokeswoman said Superclub had 60 shops in Belgium, 22 in the Netherlands and four in France.

Last month Philips said management of its Videoland chain, formerly part of Superclub, was buying out the 187-shop chain, part of a strategy announced last October by incoming chairman Cor Boonstra to strip away non-performing or non-core units.
